narrative.overview:
The whole site is printed like the leaflet that comes in a flat-pack box: wordless outline drawings, circled numerals, a parts list that is the price list, and a warning box where the honest caveats go. It is set in two inks on one paper. Black line ink draws every object and every rule; ultramarine is a printed field that owns whole regions of the sheet rather than decorating small things. Nothing is photographed and nothing glows, because there is nothing real to photograph yet and the system refuses to pretend otherwise.

Dirt is the only third colour, and it is a material, not an accent: warm-brown halftone dots on a 45° screen whose density is the amount of dirt. Clean is white. The hero sofa is drawn white under a layer of dirt dots; scrubbing removes dots and reveals white fabric, so the state of the object is carried by tone, not by labels or colour-coding. The same logic runs through the step drawings and the stain samples.

Density is calm and editorial: generous section padding, long hairline-ruled lists, content set on a 12-column feel with asymmetric splits (7/5, 4/8, 6/5). The system explicitly rejects the cleaning-category default of white and mint gradients, bubbles, sparkles and stock photos of a smiling worker.
keyCharacteristics: Paper ground everywhere; ultramarine as whole printed fields (parts-list sheet, contact, footer), never as tinted bands.
One pen: outline drawings at a single contour weight with non-scaling strokes.
Halftone dots are the only way dirt appears; white fill is the only way clean appears.
Structure from 1.5px ink hairlines, not from cards, shadows or background changes.
Circled ink numerals for sequence and for callouts pinned to the object by leader lines.
Flat print: no gradients, no glass, no shadows of any kind.

rules.name: The Paper Ground Rule
rules.body: Paper is the only ground. A section never gets a tinted background band; if it needs separating, it gets a 1.5px ink hairline. The only non-paper grounds are full ultramarine fields.

rules.name: The White Means Clean Rule
rules.body: White is never a surface for layout. It is the colour of clean fabric in drawings, the well of an input, and the hover lift of a paper control. Anything else white is a mistake.

rules.name: The Field, Not Accent Rule
rules.body: Ultramarine is printed as a field that owns a region edge to edge. It is not used for chips, badges, icon tints or decorative strokes on paper; on paper it only marks interaction state.

rules.name: The Dirt Is Dots Rule
rules.body: The dirt colour describes dirt and only dirt, as halftone dots whose density is the state (a thin dirt stroke only where the dirt is itself a line, such as hair). It is never a background, a text colour, or a decorative accent.

rules.name: The Validation-Only Red Rule
rules.body: Red exists for invalid form fields and their status message. It is never used for emphasis, prices, warnings or stains (the warning box is ink).

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Unbounded speaks for anything that is a name, a number or a command: headings, buttons, prices, totals, numerals, nav on mobile. Onest speaks for anything that is read. Never set a paragraph in Unbounded.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change or be compared (prices, quantities, totals, the cleaned percentage, district fees) uses tabular figures so columns and live updates do not jitter.

rules.name: The Hairline, Not Band Rule
rules.body: Sections, lists and strips are separated by 1.5px ink hairlines (heavy edges at 2px, row dividers at 1px Pencil Rule). Background colour changes are reserved for whole ultramarine fields.

rules.name: The One Strip Rule
rules.body: A sequence of instruction panels is one strip, ruled top and bottom and split by vertical hairlines. Never wrap steps in individual cards.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Everything is printed in black line and ultramarine field on paper, plus dirt dots. No gradients, no translucent glass, no drop or offset shadows. If something needs to stand forward, give it a heavier line or put it on an ink field.

rules.name: The One Pen Rule
rules.body: Every drawing, icon and logo is outline-only at one contour weight with non-scaling strokes. Fills are only white (clean fabric) or halftone (dirt). No filled pictograms, no duotone icons, no glyph icons.

rules.name: The Pinned Label Rule
rules.body: Labels about an object are pinned to it: a circled ink numeral in the legend and a leader line ending in a dot on the drawing, or a numbered pin on the drawing itself on small screens. Labels do not float in badges over the art.

dos: Do keep paper (`#f5f5f0`) as the only ground and separate sections with 1.5px ink hairlines.
Do give ultramarine whole regions (the parts-list sheet, contact, deep ultramarine footer) and let the parts-list field bleed to the viewport edge.
Do draw dirt only as warm-brown halftone dots on a 45° screen, with density carrying the amount of dirt, and draw clean as white fill.
Do draw every object and icon outline-only at one contour weight (2px, 2.4px on the hero) with non-scaling strokes.
Do number sequences and callouts with circled ink numerals and pin labels to the object with leader lines ending in a dot.
Do set instruction panels in one strip split by hairlines.
Do use Unbounded with tabular figures for every price, quantity and total.
donts: Don't use white + mint gradients, bubbles, sparkles or stock photos of a smiling worker.
Don't use gradients, glass, blur, or drop and offset shadows; the system is two inks on paper.
Don't tint section backgrounds or put content in floating cards; use hairlines and ink fields.
Don't use the dirt colour for anything that is not dirt, or white as a layout surface.
Don't use red for anything except form validation.
Don't use filled, duotone or glyph icons; draw them in the same pen as the furniture.
Don't invent photos, ratings, counts or testimonials to fill a visual slot; illustrations stay plainly drawn.
